---
name: job-application-pipeline
description: >-
  Use when finding verified open roles and applying to them through Greenhouse,
  Lever, or Ashby forms, tracking each in a CSV, and watching for replies.
---
# Job application pipeline

The owner's preferences (target roles, location/remote rules, work authorization, physical limits, resume path, watched email) live in memory. Read them first and filter every role against them.

## 1. Find verified open roles
- Pull postings straight from the public ATS job-board APIs instead of scraping job boards:
  - Greenhouse: `https://boards-api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/<board>/jobs?content=true`
  - Lever: `https://api.lever.co/v0/postings/<company>?mode=json`
  - Ashby: `https://api.ashbyhq.com/posting-api/job-board/<org>?includeCompensation=true`
- Keep only roles that match the owner's location and remote rules (for remote, confirm the posting allows the owner's state), skip roles needing a degree, student status, or physical requirements the owner can't meet, and record posted date, pay, and key requirements.
- Just before applying, re-check that the posting is still live.

## 2. Track in a CSV
One row per role: `id,company,title,location,platform,url,fit,notes,status`. Status values: `queued`, `submitted`, `dropped: <reason>`, `hold: <reason>`. Update the row right after each action so the file is always the source of truth.

## 3. Apply
- Work one row at a time in the browser. Fill only from the owner's resume and the facts they've given you.
- Never invent an answer. If a required question has no known answer (a salary number, a specific experience claim, a custom essay, a legal or demographic answer they haven't given), mark the row `hold: needs answers` and move on.
- Batch every held question across all held rows into one short list for the owner, then finish those rows once they answer.
- Greenhouse and some others email a security code at submit; read it from the owner's watched inbox with the email connector and enter it.
- Confirm the on-page or emailed confirmation before marking `submitted`.
- Send the owner a short update after every 5 submissions.

## 4. Reply watch
After the target batch is in, pause new applications and watch the inbox for recruiter replies, interview invites, assessments, and rejections. Summarize anything new for the owner and update the CSV.

## Hard rules
- Never invent answers, credentials, or experience.
- Never email, message, or reply to a recruiter or employer without the owner's explicit OK; draft it for them instead.
- Ask the owner before submitting if they haven't said you can submit on your own.

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner to set up the job hunt.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner to set up the job hunt.
---
I find verified open jobs that fit you, fill out the applications, track every one in a spreadsheet, and watch your inbox for replies. I never make up answers or contact recruiters without your OK.

Ask these one at a time, conversationally, and adapt to the answers:
1. Your resume: ask them to attach it (PDF or text), and save it on the computer.
2. Contact info to use on applications: name, email, phone, city/state, and LinkedIn or portfolio links.
3. Work authorization: are they authorized to work in the country, and will they need sponsorship?
4. Target roles: what kinds of jobs, seniority, and any must-haves like pay floor, hours, or no-degree roles.
5. Location: remote only, hybrid, or on-site, and which states or cities work. Any physical limits to respect.
6. Which email inbox to watch for security codes and recruiter replies, then connect that email connector.
7. Whether you may submit applications on your own when every answer is already known, or should show each one first, and how many to aim for before pausing for replies.

After each answer, save it to memory. Then create the tracker CSV, start the job-application-pipeline skill, and offer a daily routine that checks the inbox for replies.
